store: Grid emission factors — PCAF Part A, renewable generation
note: Two bases are held per country and they are not interchangeable. The grid average is what a consumer draws (used for the project's own scope 2). The combined margin is what a new grid-connected renewable displaces (used for avoided emissions) and is what CDM Tool 07 requires. Substituting one for the other changes the answer materially while looking correct, so where a basis is not held it is reported absent rather than filled from the other silently.

bases.gridAverage: Average emission intensity of electricity supplied — the consumption basis.
bases.combinedMargin: CDM combined margin (operating margin and build margin, weighted) — the displacement basis for grid-connected renewables.

gridAverage.source: Ceylon Electricity Board, Long Term Generation Expansion Plan 2023-2042
gridAverage.flagNote: Read from the LTGEP planning infographic, which states the average factor falling from about 0.5 to 0.2 kg/kWh by 2042. Confirm the published annual figure with CEB before disclosure.

combinedMargin.source: National Grid Emission Factor, calculated with the UNFCCC Tool to calculate the emission factor for an electricity system v02.2.1. Operating margin 0.9224 tCO2/MWh.
combinedMargin.publisher: DNA Sri Lanka / Climate Change Division and Sri Lanka Sustainable Energy Authority
combinedMargin.flagNote: Published against Energy Balance 2017. The generation mix has moved materially since, so this factor is nine years old and should be refreshed with SLSEA before it supports a disclosed figure.

solarCapacityFactor.basis: Global horizontal irradiance of roughly 5.0-5.5 kWh/m2/day

countries.name: Singapore

gridAverage.source: Grid Emission Factor, average operating margin. Fell from 0.412 in 2023 on a higher solar share and reduced coal.

countries.combinedMarginAbsentReason: EMA publishes the operating margin and the build margin separately but no combined-margin figure is held here. Obtain and weight them per CDM Tool 07 before an avoided-emissions figure is disclosed.

solarCapacityFactor.basis: Equatorial irradiance with high cloud cover; constrained rooftop and floating siting

countries.name: Norway

gridAverage.source: Location-based factor for physically delivered electricity. 15 gCO2e/kWh in 2023 and 19 in 2022; about 95% of consumption renewable.

countries.combinedMarginAbsentReason: No CDM combined margin is held for Norway. On a hydro-dominated system the displaced factor is very low and highly sensitive to whether the market boundary is Norwegian or Nordic, which is a modelling decision this store will not make on the reporting entity's behalf.

solarCapacityFactor.basis: High latitude; strong seasonal swing with negligible winter yield

countries.name: Uganda
countries.gridAverageAbsentReason: No national average consumption factor is held. The standardized baseline publishes margins for project displacement, not a consumption factor.

combinedMargin.source: Combined margin for wind and solar power generation project activities. Operating margin 0.2740 tCO2/MWh; build margin 0.00001 tCO2/MWh, effectively nil because every unit in the build margin sample was hydro or solar.
combinedMargin.publisher: UNFCCC CDM standardized baseline ASB0054-2022, 10 August 2022

solarCapacityFactor.basis: Equatorial plateau; high irradiance with low seasonal variation

auxiliaryConsumption.note: Parasitic load of a utility-scale photovoltaic plant — inverters, trackers, monitoring, security and night-time station service — typically 0.5% to 1% of gross generation. The low end is applied. Replace with metered auxiliary consumption where it exists, which is what moves this from an assumption to a measurement.
